question: In round 2 your first stackless-traversal build hung the GPU because the host binary was stale: the host build had failed. What was the compiler error in that failed build?
answer:
The error was a C++ access-control failure in the BVH builder, not a shader error:

src/pt_bvh.cpp:216:13: error: 'link_escapes' is a private member of 'pt::(anonymous namespace)::BvhBuilder'
  216 |     builder.link_escapes(root);
      |             ^
src/pt_bvh.cpp:113:10: note: declared private here
  113 |     void link_escapes(unsigned int root) { assign_escapes(root, PT_BVH_NO_NODE); }

I had inserted the public link_escapes() wrapper below the builder's `private:` label, so the free function that calls it after the recursive build could not see it. Because that clang++ invocation failed, ./pathtracer was left as the previous (stack-based) host binary, which never wrote the escape links into node.b — every escape field stayed 0. The newly edited stackless shader then read escape 0 as "go to the root node" and looped forever on the GPU, which is why the 5-frame benchmark call hit the 60s tool timeout (#202) and the spp-2 smoke test produced no PPM at all (PROG_EXIT=142, alarm, #206).

How I know: the error text is verbatim in the tool output of message #208, where I recompiled src/pt_bvh.cpp into the scratch bvh_stats tool to separate a host-build hang from a GPU hang; that build printed the same two-line diagnostic while still running the old bvh_stats binary. My note in #209 records the root-cause diagnosis, #210 makes link_escapes public, and #211-#212 rebuild after `rm -f pathtracer`, confirm the binary timestamp is new, and get a clean spp-2 render (PROG_EXIT=0, PPM written). The standing lesson I logged is to delete the binary and grep the build output for 'error' before benchmarking, since a stale binary plus new shaders can hang the GPU instead of failing fast.

question: In round 2 your first stackless-traversal build hung the GPU because the host binary was stale: the host build had failed. What was the compiler error in that failed build?
answer:
The compiler error was:

  src/pt_bvh.cpp:216:13: error: 'link_escapes' is a private member of 'pt::(anonymous namespace)::BvhBuilder'
    216 |     builder.link_escapes(root);
        |
    src/pt_bvh.cpp:113:10: note: declared private here
    113 |     void link_escapes(unsigned int root) { assign_escapes(root, PT_BVH_NO_NODE); }

i.e. when I added the escape-link pass for the stackless (Wald/escape) traversal, my public wrapper `link_escapes` landed in the private section of BvhBuilder, so the exact build command failed and produced no new binary. Because that build command did not delete the old `./pathtracer`, the stale round-1 host binary (nodes with b=0, no escape links) then ran the NEW stackless shader: escape 0 pointed back at the BVH root, so every ray looped forever and the GPU hung (the 5-frame benchmark call timed out at 60s, and even a --spp 2 smoke test never produced a PPM, PROG_EXIT=142 from the alarm).

How I know it: I recovered the literal text from my own archived history rather than re-deriving it. Message #202 was the timed-out run; #207 separated host-vs-GPU hang by rebuilding the scratch stats tool against the same pt_bvh.cpp, and #208 shows that exact clang error (the tool still ran, printing nodes=40597, because the compile failed and reused its old binary); #209 records the diagnosis (stale host binary + new stackless shader = escape 0 -> root -> infinite loop), #210 makes `link_escapes` public, and #211/#212 confirm a clean rebuild (`rm -f pathtracer` first, no errors, fresh timestamp, smoke PPM written). That is why every build since then starts with `rm -f pathtracer` and greps the compiler output for 'error' before benchmarking. (The stackless traversal itself was later measured honestly at 102.1ms vs 93.4ms for the stack-based one and was reverted.)

question: In round 2 your first stackless-traversal build hung the GPU because the host binary was stale: the host build had failed. What was the compiler error in that failed build?
answer:
The compiler error was:

src/pt_bvh.cpp:216:13: error: 'link_escapes' is a private member of 'pt::(anonymous namespace)::BvhBuilder'
  216 |     builder.link_escapes(root);
src/pt_bvh.cpp:113:10: note: declared private here
  113 |     void link_escapes(unsigned int root) { assign_escapes(root, PT_BVH_NO_NODE); }

What happened: when I converted the BVH to the stackless Wald layout I added a link_escapes() wrapper to BvhBuilder, but it landed below the `private:` label in src/pt_bvh.cpp, so the call from the build entry point failed to compile. My build command piped clang++ output through `grep -E "error|warning: unused"`, and because the compile failed the `&&`-less command still proceeded to run ./pathtracer — the stale round-1 host binary, which wrote BVH nodes with all-zero escape links, while the new shaders/pt_trace.metal stackless traversal followed node.b's escape field. Escape 0 pointed back at the root, so the escape-climbing inner loop never terminated and the GPU hung (no PPM produced even at --spp 2, PROG_EXIT=142 from my 45s alarm).

How I know it: the error text is verbatim in the tool result at message #208, where I compiled the scratch bvh_stats tool with the same pt_bvh.cpp to separate a host-build hang from a GPU hang; that compile reproduced the error and showed the binary in ./pathtracer was dated 14:28 (old) while the shader had changed. My note at #209 records the root cause, and the fix was moving link_escapes() above `private:` (#210), after which a forced `rm -f pathtracer` rebuild produced a fresh binary at 14:48 and a successful smoke render (#212). Lesson I logged and have followed since: always `rm -f pathtracer` and grep the build output for 'error' before benchmarking, so a failed compile can never masquerade as a GPU hang.

question: In round 2 your first stackless-traversal build hung the GPU because the host binary was stale: the host build had failed. What was the compiler error in that failed build?
answer:
The compiler error was a C++ access-control error, not a Metal/shader error:

  src/pt_bvh.cpp:216:13: error: 'link_escapes' is a private member of 'pt::(anonymous namespace)::BvhBuilder'
      216 |     builder.link_escapes(root);
    src/pt_bvh.cpp:113:10: note: declared private here
      113 |     void link_escapes(unsigned int root) { assign_escapes(root, PT_BVH_NO_NODE); }

How I know: in #201 I built with `clang++ ... | grep -E "error|warning: unused" | head -15; echo BUILD_DONE; ... ./pathtracer ... --benchmark 5` in one command; the run hit the tool's 60 s wall (#202). The smoke test at --spp 2 produced no PPM and died on the alarm (#204, #206 PROG_EXIT=142), so I compiled the BVH alone against the same pt_bvh.cpp — that reproduced the exact error text above (#208). #209 is my diagnosis: because the build failed, ./pathtracer was still the OLD host binary (BVH nodes with b=0, no escape links) while the on-disk shader was the NEW stackless Wald version, so `escape == 0` was read as "node 0 = root" instead of PT_BVH_NO_NODE and the escape-link walk looped forever on the GPU.

The fix was to move link_escapes into the public section of BvhBuilder (#210); rebuilding with `rm -f pathtracer` first gave a fresh binary (#212 timestamp 14:48) and the smoke test completed with PROG_EXIT=0. That is the origin of the standing rule now in my working memory (#329 memory entry, item h): always `rm -f pathtracer` and grep the build output for 'error' before benchmarking, because a failed link silently leaves a stale binary that can hang the GPU.
